name: Sunken Vault

detectability.signature: Broadband energy emission across visible and ultraviolet spectra, manifesting as a shifting luminous haze with periodic flare events detectable on hyperspace resonance scanners

proximity: Hyperspace navigation drives register false transit echoes, complicating jump calculations
Hull surfaces accumulate a faint static charge that interferes with external sensor arrays
Crew members near exterior bulkheads report tingling sensations and mild nausea
contact: Direct exposure to bleed energy causes catastrophic overloads in unshielded hyperspace drives
Electrical systems experience cascading surges that can disable entire power grids
Organic tissue exposed to concentrated bleed radiation develops cellular anomalies within hours
prolonged_exposure: Hyperspace drives permanently lose calibration, requiring full replacement rather than repair
Cumulative energy absorption raises hull temperature to dangerous levels, eventually compromising structural alloys
Long-term biological effects include neural pathway disruption and persistent sensory hallucinations

age: First recorded 1,200 years ago, but geological evidence from a nearby planetoid suggests energy scarring consistent with at least 10,000 years of activity

behavior.cycle: Major flare events occur on an irregular cycle averaging 73 standard days, with minor fluctuations in luminosity on a near-constant basis

phenomena: Luminous tendrils of hyperspace energy extend outward from the core region, writhing slowly like the arms of some submerged creature reaching through a membrane
During flare events, the visible boundary expands by up to fifteen percent and briefly reveals geometric structures within the glow that do not correspond to any known physical objects
Vessels transiting nearby in hyperspace report a sensation of resistance, as though the fabric of that domain has been thinned or torn

Electromagnetic interference within the field produces patterns on communication arrays that some analysts have controversially described as structured, though no linguistic content has been confirmed
hazards: Hyperspace drive overload during flare events, with a risk of uncontrolled micro-jumps
Cumulative radiation exposure from bleed energy, which is not fully mitigated by standard shielding
Unpredictable expansion of the active boundary during major flare cycles
opportunities: The bleed energy can be harvested using modified collector arrays, providing a potent if unstable fuel source for hyperspace-capable vessels
Study of the membrane breach offers insights into the fundamental nature of hyperspace and may lead to advances in transit technology
The geometric structures visible during flare events are of intense interest to archaeo-physicists who believe they may be artifacts of an ancient hyperspace-capable civilization
known_incidents: The survey frigate Cartographer's Lantern suffered a catastrophic hyperspace drive detonation in 3171 when a flare event caught it within the active boundary, destroying the vessel and creating a debris field that remains suspended in the bleed energy

An unauthorized energy-harvesting operation by the Sable Compact in 3198 extracted an estimated 14 terawatt-hours of bleed energy before a boundary expansion forced evacuation; three of their collector platforms were never recovered
description: Sunken Vault appears as a wound in the fabric of space, a vast and irregular luminosity that shifts between pale violet and searing white depending on the observer's angle and the anomaly's current state of agitation. The glow has no clean edges. Instead it fades outward in tendrils and filaments that curl and retract like the slow breathing of something immense and half-submerged. At its core, the light is too bright and too wrong for comfortable observation, carrying wavelengths that standard filters struggle to categorize.

The energy bleeding through the breach behaves unlike any conventional radiation. It interferes with hyperspace drives on a fundamental level, inducing resonance patterns that can overload motivator coils and corrupt navigation matrices. During the anomaly's periodic flare events, the output intensifies dramatically, and the visible boundary swells outward as though something on the other side is pressing against a thinning membrane. Vessels caught within the expanded zone during a flare report systems failures, hallucinations among crew, and in the worst cases, brief uncontrolled translations into hyperspace.

The name Sunken Vault was coined by the explorer Maren Adzic, who described the anomaly in her logs as resembling a great vault or treasury that had sunk beneath the surface of reality, its light still visible through the water above. The metaphor has persisted. Theories about its origin range from a natural weakness in the hyperspace membrane to the remnant of an ancient transit gate that catastrophically failed. The geometric structures glimpsed during flare events lend some credibility to the latter hypothesis, though no conclusive evidence has been recovered.

Sunken Vault is currently ringed by a cordon of automated warning buoys maintained by the Navigational Hazard Authority. A dedicated monitoring station, Vigil Platform, tracks flare cycles from a safe distance of 1.8 million kilometers and broadcasts predictive alerts to transiting vessels. Interest in the anomaly has intensified recently following the discovery that bleed energy samples exhibit quantum coherence patterns not found in any known natural phenomenon, raising uncomfortable questions about what, exactly, is on the other side of the breach.
